newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-PORTUGAL REFEREE CHIEF RESIGNS AMID BRIBERY SCANDAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PORTUGAL REFEREE CHIEF RESIGNS AMID BRIBERY SCANDAL.

text.p: The head of Portugal's referees organisation stepped down on Friday amid a nationwide soccer scandal that has left many Portuguese feeling that their favourite sport is corrupt to the core.
The president of the Portuguese Football League's Council of Referees, judge Jose Cruz Pereira, announced his resignation at a meeting of top league officials aimed at cleaning up the game.

"You don't preach honesty, you practice it," said Cruz Pereira, who is under a judicial investigation after he admitted he had asked police to spy on a club chairman whom he suspected of bribing a referee.

Allegations of bribery and match-fixing involving club directors and referees have made front-page news for the last two weeks, prompting 40 intellectuals to announce on Thursday they had switched allegiance from their Portuguese clubs to Spanish league leaders Barcelona.
"We've all changed our wives or husbands, our political parties and our jobs but never our clubs," the group, known as the 'Barcelona Faction', wrote in a statement.
On Wednesday a court sentenced the chairman of first division side Leca and a former referee to prison for bribery following a major match-rigging investigation.
An investigation is currently under way into allegations that Portuguese champions Porto sought to bribe a referee 12 years ago before a European Cup-Winners Cup match against Scotland's Aberdeen.
Both Porto and the Romanian referee in charge of the game have denied the charges.
Porto, who have qualified for the quarter-finals of this season's European Champions Cup, are embroiled in another controversy over the payment for a holiday in Brazil last year for another referee.
Justice Minister Jose Vera Jardim said on Thursday there were 10 soccer corruption cases pending.
Top Lisbon team Benfica have proposed the introduction of a referee lottery system under which officials for matches would be decided by a draw broadcast live on television.
